scope_summary: Per-failure root-cause + file-touch + harness-deletion plan for the 9 HTTP conformance failures. Phases 02-06 of STATE.md each consume one or more nodes here. Stdio currently passes only because tools/conformance_runner.py:766-1127 hand-rolls the missing semantics. Every fix lands the real-wire behavior AND deletes the masking simulator branch.

verified_assumptions.claim: BackingStore.send signature does NOT accept reply_to
verified_assumptions.evidence: packages/python/src/sox_protocol/core/ports/backing_store.py:73-112 — async def send(channel, sender, body, correlation_id=None) -> tuple[str, float, int, BackpressureInfo]. No reply_to parameter.

verified_assumptions.claim: MemoryStore._StoredMessage already has a reply_to field but no path delivers a value
verified_assumptions.evidence: packages/python/src/sox_protocol/adapters/backing_stores/memory/store.py:41 (reply_to: str | None = None) and :55 (to_wire emits reply_to). MemoryStore.send (line 119-159) constructs _StoredMessage WITHOUT setting reply_to.
packages/python/src/sox_protocol/core/middleware/plugins/store_dispatch.py:100-121 — only channel, sender, body, correlation_id are extracted before calling self._store.send(...).

verified_assumptions.claim: spec/operations/group_invite.output.schema.json mandates {invited, agent_id, invited_at}; fixture mandates {group_id, invited_agent, invited_at}

verified_assumptions.claim: BackingStore.send already passes msg.reply_to=None as wire default and stdio's harness simulator (line 996-1036) hand-attaches reply_to to the in-memory _StoredMessage before append
verified_assumptions.evidence: tools/conformance_runner.py:1000 reads args['reply_to']; line 1023 sets msg.reply_to via setattr. This is the masking simulation.

verified_assumptions.claim: SQLite store has reply_to=None hard-coded in to_wire equivalent
verified_assumptions.evidence: packages/python/src/sox_protocol/adapters/backing_stores/sqlite/store.py:61 — "reply_to": None as a static dict literal.

verified_assumptions.claim: BackingStore.replay impls in both stores DO honor 'since' end-to-end with the correct comparator
verified_assumptions.evidence: memory/store.py:378-392 filters m.seq >= since and sorts; sqlite/store.py:603-628 issues a SQL WHERE seq >= ? predicate. The implementation is sound; the failure must be at the wire-protocol field naming layer (fixture sends 'since_seq', spec input requires 'since').
spec/operations/replay.input.schema.json required: ['channel','since','limit']. The fixtures use since_seq (replay/01-replay-since-seq.yaml:63 'since_seq: 3'; replay/02:45 'since_seq: 999').
packages/python/src/sox_protocol/adapters/backing_stores/memory/store.py:279-302 — adds agent_id to msg.delivered_to for matching channels, returns (removed, pending_cleared).

verified_assumptions.claim: Stdio tool surface uses key 'patterns' for unsubscribe input; spec uses 'channels'
verified_assumptions.evidence: core/mcp_server/tools.py:273 channels__unsubscribe(patterns: list[str]); spec unsubscribe.input.schema.json required ['channels']. The HTTP route at routes.py:380-403 already supports both via the middleware (store_dispatch.py:151 inp.get('channels', inp.get('patterns', []))) and remaps removed→unsubscribed at line 402-403.

verified_assumptions.claim: list_channels HTTP route already injects _sox_protocol block
verified_assumptions.evidence: packages/python/src/sox_protocol/adapters/transports/http/routes.py:426-435 augments response with _sox_protocol block when missing. But fixture also requires top-level protocol_version (yaml line 20: 'protocol_version: {{any_string}}').

verified_assumptions.claim: HTTP heartbeat does NOT emit a sox/presence event; only the harness simulator does
verified_assumptions.evidence: MemoryStore.heartbeat (memory/store.py:319-339) updates self._liveness only; no message append. tools/conformance_runner.py:1072-1108 hand-builds a presence_body and appends a _StoredMessage on channel='sox/presence' (the masking simulation).

verified_assumptions.claim: Fixture unsubscribe expected_output uses key 'unsubscribed'; HTTP route already remaps removed→unsubscribed
verified_assumptions.evidence: routes.py:399-403; subscription-patterns/02-unsubscribe-discards-queue.yaml:38 'unsubscribed: {{any_array}}'. So the unsubscribe failure mode is NOT the field-name remap — it's that pending messages are not actually discarded for THIS fixture path. Need investigation of the recv-after-unsubscribe path: MemoryStore impl does discard via delivered_to set; the simulator at 976-994 also discards. Hypothesis: subscriber_count or recv path is fine on memory store; failure must be in the SqliteStore's unsubscribe — but HTTP runs against MemoryStore via SharedMemoryTarget? Re-check: HTTP uses ProcessHttpTarget (subprocess) which spawns the http server which uses MemoryStore by default. Need phase 04 agent to bisect via direct fixture run.

tasks.v1_scope_anchor: docs/V1-SCOPE.md:22 (replay row) — 'Replay historical messages from a channel using a per-channel seq cursor. Parameters: channel, since (seq), until (seq or null), limit'.
tasks.root_cause_hypothesis: Wire-protocol field-name mismatch: fixture sends 'since_seq' but spec/operations/replay.input.schema.json requires 'since'. The HTTP route at routes.py:572-584 forwards body verbatim to the pipeline; StoreDispatchMiddleware.replay branch (store_dispatch.py:217-232) reads inp.get('since', 0) — so since_seq is silently treated as 0 and ALL messages are returned (4 instead of expected 2). Stdio passes only because the harness simulator (conformance_runner.py:1110-1126) reads args.get('since_seq', 0). FIX-TARGET: spec — the fixture is correct in INTENT but uses an outdated parameter name; canonical spec says 'since'. Update the fixture YAML to use 'since: 3' (and fixture 02 to use 'since: 999'). Alternative fix-target: accept both 'since' and 'since_seq' in the input schema as a transitional alias — REJECTED: spec/operations/replay.input.schema.json has additionalProperties default-false on the parent, and adding aliases pollutes a v1 contract. Spec wins; fixture is the loser.

tasks.v1_scope_anchor: docs/V1-SCOPE.md:21 (heartbeat row) — 'Triggers events on sox/presence'; spec/primitives/presence.md §5 — 'The server emits presence-change events on the reserved sox/presence channel'.
tasks.root_cause_hypothesis: MemoryStore.heartbeat (memory/store.py:319-339) and SqliteStore.heartbeat (sqlite/store.py:545+) update only the liveness table; they do NOT append a sox/presence message. The spec says the server emits coalesced state-transition events on sox/presence with body shape {event, agent_id, state, changed_at}. The harness simulator at conformance_runner.py:1072-1108 hand-rolls this emit. FIX: both stores' heartbeat impls must, on a state transition (or on every call for v1 — coalescing is post-v1 per spec.md hint), append a _StoredMessage on channel='sox/presence' with sender='__server__' and the documented body shape, then set _new_message_event so subscribers see it via recv. Then delete the simulator's emit logic.

(2) HTTP route already injects _sox_protocol (routes.py:426-435), so the assertion against _sox_protocol will pass once the fixture is corrected. The simulator's protocol_version top-level field is masking the spec/fixture mismatch. FIX-TARGET: both. Spec output schema has additionalProperties:false → cannot add protocol_version. Fix the fixture to assert _sox_protocol structure.

risk_register.summary: BackingStore.send signature change is breaking: every concrete store + every test that calls store.send() directly must update. There are at least 3 store impls (memory, filesystem, sqlite) plus the simulator + numerous unit tests.
risk_register.mitigation: Add reply_to with a default of None — preserves backward compatibility for all positional and keyword call-sites that don't pass it. Use kwarg-only via *, reply_to=None to prevent accidental positional misuse.

risk_register.summary: Heartbeat side-effect (sox/presence emit) introduces a write-on-every-call pattern that may interact with backpressure or watch loops in unexpected ways. Spec §5 hints at coalescing as post-v1.
risk_register.mitigation: v1 emits one event per call (no coalescing). Use sender='__server__' to avoid identity verification on the synthetic message. Verify the existing reserved-prefix ACL doesn't reject server-emitted writes.

risk_register.summary: Phase 04 (unsubscribe) hypothesis is two-part — the actual root cause requires verification by running the fixture with diagnostic logging. SqliteStore.unsubscribe was not directly read in this planning pass.
risk_register.mitigation: Phase 04 agent's first action: read sqlite/store.py unsubscribe and reproduce via direct conformance run. If MemoryStore is correct, SqliteStore is the suspect.

risk_register.summary: Phase 06 group_invite output shape change may break downstream consumers (TUI, claude_code runtime) if they read invited_agent or group_id from the response.
risk_register.mitigation: Grep for 'invited_agent' and 'group_id' as group_invite response keys before changing impl. If any consumers exist, migrate them in the same commit.
